/compare/.description: A quick checklist before you give your dog a long-lasting chew like a bully stick, yak cheese chew, beef cheek roll or antler: supervise, pick a size and hardness that suits your dog (follow the brand's size guidance), remove small or broken pieces, keep water available, and ask your vet. transcript: Before you give your dog a long-lasting chew, like a bully stick, yak chew or antler, run through this quick checklist.
One. Supervise your dog while it chews.
Two. Choose a size and hardness that suits your dog, and follow the brand's size guidance.
For example, Best Bully Sticks says to choose a bully stick that's wider than your dog's mouth, and when in doubt, select a larger size.
Three. Take away small or broken pieces. Four. Keep fresh water available.
Five. Ask your vet if a chew is right for your dog, especially for puppies, seniors, dogs with dental work, or dogs on special diets.
Then check what the brand actually says: the ingredients, where it says the chew is made and sourced, and its size and supervision notes.
Nibbables compares 34 chews from 12 brands, quoting each brand's own page, with sources. We don't rate safety. Find it at nibbables dot com.

transcript: How long do you microwave a yak chew? Here's what the brands' own instructions say.
First, the instructions we found all describe the leftover end piece, not a whole chew.
Times run from 30 to 90 seconds. Himalayan Dog Chew and Pawstruck say 45 seconds. Mighty Paw says 45 to 60. Yak Chewz says 60, and not more than 90, due to burning.
Soak it first? Himalayan Dog Chew, Yak Chewz, Mighty Paw and Yakkity Zac's say about five minutes. Pawstruck and Yakers don't mention it.
Every source says to let it cool before your dog gets it. Mighty Paw and Himalayan Pet Supply also say to supervise.
All seven sources, quoted word for word, are at nibbables dot com. Follow the brand you bought, and ask your vet if you're unsure.

/how-long-do-bully-sticks-last/.description: Do bully sticks go bad? Only 4 of 18 bully stick product pages state a shelf life (Redbarn and Pawstruck: 36 months; Bully Bunches: 1-2 years; Jack&Pup: months). Natural Farm lists mold and a sour or ammonia-like smell as signs to discard. Brands disagree on refrigerating a chewed stick, and Redbarn says to discard it once it can be swallowed whole. Brand pages checked 2026-10-26.
/how-long-do-bully-sticks-last/.caption: A short summary of this page (brand pages and guides checked 2026-10-26). These are the brands' claims, not ours. Narration is computer-generated.
transcript: Do bully sticks go bad? Here's what eighteen product pages and four seller guides say.
Only four of the eighteen product pages state a shelf life. Redbarn and Pawstruck say thirty-six months. Bully Bunches says one to two years. Jack and Pup says months.
Natural Farm's guide says to throw one out if it has fuzzy white, green or black spots, or a sour or ammonia-like smell.
Storing a chewed stick? Brands disagree. Redbarn says air dry it and don't refrigerate. Natural Farm and Bully Sticks Direct say refrigerate it.
And the last piece? Redbarn says take it away once it can be swallowed whole, about two and a half to three inches in most cases.
Every brand's exact wording is at nibbables dot com. Check the date on your bag, follow the brand you bought, and ask your vet if you're unsure.

transcript: Bully stick or collagen stick? Three brands sell both, so here's what their own pages say.
All three bully sticks list beef pizzle as the one ingredient. The collagen sticks list beef collagen, or in Best Bully Sticks' case, beef hide as the source of collagen.
Jack and Pup lists at least ninety percent protein for its collagen stick and seventy-five for its bully stick, with minimum fat of half a percent versus fourteen and a half.
Raw Paws is the only brand that gives an origin for both. Turkey for the bully stick, Colombia for the collagen stick.
Which lasts longer? We found no study comparing them. Best Bully Sticks calls its collagen stick long-lasting for strong chewers, while Jack and Pup rates both for moderate chewers.

transcript: We read the size advice on forty-seven dog chew product pages. Fifteen never name a dog size or a chewer type.

Thirteen of those give one rule instead. Best Bully Sticks says always choose a bully stick that's wider than your dog's mouth, to avoid accidental swallowing. Earth Animal says, when in doubt, size up.

Small dog or puppy? Raw Paws calls its thin six-inch bully sticks ideal for small dogs and puppies, and Nature Gnaws says the same about its small six-inch sticks. Seven pages mention puppies, twelve mention small dogs.
Power chewer? Mighty Paw recommends thick sticks for heavy chewers and jumbo for aggressive chewers. Redbarn says twelve inches and up for power chewers.
Some go by weight. Mighty Paw sizes its elk antlers medium for ten to forty-five pounds, large for forty-five to seventy-five, and monster for seventy-five plus.
Whatever you pick, supervise your dog, take away small pieces, and ask your vet. All forty-seven chews, grouped by dog size in each brand's own words, are at nibbables dot com.

/bully-stick-vs-beef-tendon/.description: Bully stick vs beef tendon from five brands that sell both (Pawstruck, Redbarn, Pupford, Sancho & Lola's Closet, Nature Gnaws): bully sticks list beef pizzle, tendon chews list tendon or beef, and two tendon pages that show a USA badge also name Colombia or Paraguay as the source or country of origin. transcript: This beef tendon page says Made in the USA. Scroll down to its FAQ, and the same page says these chews are sourced in Colombia.

Most people treat bully sticks and tendons as the same beef chew. They're not. All five brands' bully sticks list beef pizzle. Pupford's tendon lists beef Achilles tendon, and Nature Gnaws' tendon wraps add beef gullet.

If you buy tendons because you want them made in the USA, read past the badge. Pupford's page shows Made in the USA, and its FAQ says sourced in Colombia. Redbarn shows Made in the USA with globally sourced ingredients, and lists country of origin, Paraguay.
Some pages just say it plainly. Sancho and Lola's Closet says its flexor tendons are made in Colorado. Pawstruck says made in Paraguay.

And which lasts longer? We found no study that measures it. Sancho and Lola's even says its USA beef tendons will not be long-lasting for larger dogs. Pupford says it depends on your dog's size and chewing.
Supervise every chew and ask your vet. All eleven chews from five brands, quoted word for word with sources, are at nibbables dot com.

transcript: Same brand, same six-inch size, two different countries. Raw Paws lists origin Turkey for its bully sticks, and origin Colombia for its gullet sticks. We put seven brands that sell both side by side.

Most people treat gullet sticks and bully sticks as the same beef chew. They come from different parts. All seven brands' bully sticks list pizzle. Their gullet chews list gullet or esophagus. Jack's Premium explains weasand is the muscle meat that surrounds the esophagus.
And here's the catch. Not every esophagus chew is just esophagus. Redbarn's collagen wrapped esophagus stick lists collagen from beef hide first, then beef esophagus.

If your dog needs a softer chew, several brands pitch gullet that way. Jack and Pup says softer and easier to chew. Raw Paws lists chew hardness, light. Which lasts longer? We found no study that measures it.
Got a puppy? Read twice. Jack and Pup's gullet page says not suitable for puppies under three months old. The same page's FAQ says puppies six months and older. Ask your vet.
Supervise every chew and ask your vet. All fourteen chews from seven brands, quoted word for word with sources, are at nibbables dot com.
